slides.headline: 1) FIND YOUR REAL RATE BEFORE THEY NAME A NUMBER
slides.body: Compensation analytics firms sell salary benchmarks to employers before any interview. Your number is often set before you walk in the door.

slides.headline: 2) DECODE WHAT THEIR SALARY RANGE ACTUALLY MEANS
slides.body: A $60,000 to $140,000 posting is designed to attract every level of candidate. Most offers land in the bottom third. The real budgeted number is narrower.

slides.headline: 3) PULL THE REAL NUMBER BEHIND THEIR RANGE
slides.body: Before your negotiation, you want one specific anchor, not a 30-point spread. One prompt finds the number the company actually budgeted for this seat.

slides.headline: YOUR OFFER WAS CALCULATED
slides.body: Per MarketWatch this week: employers are using your personal data to calculate the lowest salary you'll accept. Not a guess, a model built on your financial history and how urgently you need income.

slides.headline: 4) WRITE THE COUNTER-OFFER THEY CAN'T DISMISS
slides.body: Most people counter with a gut number and hope. This prompt builds the argument from market data they didn't model when they wrote your offer.

slides.headline: 5) FIND THE HIDDEN CLAUSES THAT CUT YOUR PAY
slides.body: Clawback provisions, vesting cliffs, and non-solicitation terms reduce your effective salary. Most people sign without noticing. Claude reads the whole letter in under a minute.

slides.headline: 6) KILL THE SALARY HISTORY TRAP BEFORE IT ANCHORS YOU
slides.body: 21 states have banned asking for salary history. Interviewers still find ways to get the number, and once you give it, it becomes the floor.

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: 6 AI SALARY DEFENSE PROMPTS
slides.body:
1. Find your real rate first
2. Decode their salary range
3. Pull the real budgeted number
4. Write the counter they can't dismiss

caption:
Swipe for 6 AI prompts employers don't want you to have. 🔑 Companies are buying your personal data to calculate the lowest salary you'll accept.

Find your true market rate before they name a number, decode what the posted range actually means, pull the real budgeted number behind their range, write a counter-offer anchored to market data, find every hidden clause that cuts your pay, and kill the salary history question before it sets your anchor.

Per MarketWatch this week, employers are using personal data to reverse-engineer the lowest offer each candidate will accept. These prompts pull from the same market data and build your counter before they name a number. Running a business? DM us 'AI' and we'll show you what this could do for yours.
